title: Token economics proof plan and bench notes
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures a pragmatic proof plan for our performance + unit-economics claims (how Redwood is faster and cheaper for production LLM inference). It blends rough bench numbers, measurement methodology, required artifacts, and a prioritized evidence plan for sales collateral and field enablement. Purpose: give GTM a defensible set of claims and an actionable list of experiments we can run with Eng/Applied ML to close gaps.

Primary audiences:
- Sales (solution engineers) who need sound talking points and customer-ready artifacts.
- Growth/content for claims in docs and benchmarks.
- Engineering/applied ML for experiment coordination.

Top-level claims (draft wording):
1) Typical chat/assistant workloads: 2x–4x lower median token latency at p50 vs general cloud endpoints when using our continuous-batching + prefix cache on similar GPU classes.
2) Production throughput cases (high-concurrency): 1.5x–3x better throughput per GPU across common conversational models when using Redwood routing + batch consolidation.
3) Unit cost: 20%–45% lower $/1k tokens for long-tail, session-based apps after enabling KV caching and our quantization profiles (depends on model family and request distribution).

Important: these are ranges and must be accompanied by methodology, hardware baseline, and sample customer scenarios.

Evidence matrix (what we need):
- Microbench benches: p50/p95/p99 latency for single-request and streaming workloads using SeqLen=512/1k/2k.
- Throughput benches: tokens/sec and useful throughput for 64/128/256 concurrent sessions (sustained for 30m).
- Cost model: normalized $/1k tokens based on list instance-hour cost (public clouds) + effective tokens served.
- Real-customer sim: session replay of a 10k-user sample to show hit rate for KV/prefix cache and resulting delta in tokens generated and latency.

Benchmark methodology (keep it reproducible):
- Harness: perf-harness v0.9 (linked). Use same load-generator, deterministic prompts, and real-ish session distributions (we have standard prompt sets in github/perf-harness).
- Hardware baseline: A100-80GB equivalent (hosted) for Redwood; compare to two competitor baselines: Competitor A (multi-tenant managed endpoint on same GPU class), Competitor B (serverless-style CPU-backed variants).
- Models: pick 3 representative open/verified models (small, medium, large family) — e.g., Llama2-13B-Chat, Mistral-instruct-7B, and an LLM-70B variant. For each, run the same quantized profile where applicable.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (token and response), tokens/sec (sustained), effective $/1k tokens (with bundling of instance cost), cache hit rate, batch size distribution.
- Normalization: report per-1000-token economics and per-response latency for 256-token completion and 1k-token session.

Sample synthetic results (illustrative — NOT to publish without engineering signoff):
- Llama2-13B-Chat, 1k session, A100 baseline:
  - Redwood hosted (with KV cache + batching): p50=85ms/token, p95=240ms/token, throughput=580k tokens/hour/GPU, effective $/1k tokens=$0.09.
  - Competitor A (managed endpoint): p50=210ms/token, p95=510ms/token, throughput=210k tokens/hour/GPU, effective $/1k tokens=$0.18.
  - Competitor B (serverless): p50=340ms/token, p95=900ms/token, throughput=95k tokens/hour/GPU-equivalent, effective $/1k tokens=$0.27.
- Observations: cache + batching drives the majority of the delta on session workloads. Steady-state throughput savings translate to lower infrastructure $/token; latency improvements unlock better UX for streaming.

Use cases & messaging hooks (how sales should frame it):
- For customer with long conversational sessions: emphasize cache hit-rate benefits and show delta in $/MAU.
- For high-concurrency batch scoring (embeddings/rerank): emphasize throughput/GPU and predictable reserved capacity benefits (Dedicated).
- For regulated customers: emphasize Private deployment parity (same runtime benefits) + cost predictability.

Artifacts to produce (priority list):
1) Repro bench notebook + short readout (2 slides) showing baseline vs Redwood for Llama2-13B-Chat (highest priority).
2) Cost calculator spreadsheet for sales (inputs: model, average session length, concurrency, cache hit-rate).
3) One-pager: "How Redwood saves you money on real chat apps" with 2 quick customer scenarios and back-of-envelope math.
4) Bench packet for customers (raw results + methodology appendix).

Open questions / risks:
- Model family sensitivity: smaller models show less absolute delta from caching; need to pick conservative claims per model class.
- Hardware normalization: cloud instance pricing fluctuates; we must standardize on a transparent normalization (e.g., list on-date hourly cost for A100+ region).
- Representativeness: internal toy workloads may overfit to our batching heuristics; we must include session replay tests from 2 real customers before publishing.

Experiment plan (quick timeline):
- Week 1: Run microbench runs (single-request + streaming) for Llama2-13B-Chat and Mistral-7B across baseline and Redwood config. Responsible: Ruben, Liam. Output: bench notebook + p95 table.
- Week 2: Run throughput runs for 1h sustained at 64/128 sessions; run cost model. Responsible: Applied ML. Output: throughput numbers and normalized $/1k tokens.
- Week 3: Run session-replay sim using anonymized traces (customer opt-in). Output: cache hit-rate delta and adjusted economics.
- Week 4: Draft collateral (1-pager + 2-slide bench readout) and internal review. Responsible: Priya + Maya.

Customer narrative examples (short):
- "We cut your per-message infra footprint by ~30% for a session-based assistant by eliminating redundant token computation and consolidating batches across concurrent sessions. That means lower cloud bills and smoother streaming UX for end users."
- "For high-volume reranking, our Dedicated offering serves 1.8x the throughput per GPU vs a common managed endpoint — translate that to fewer GPUs to hit your SLA, fewer dollars spent on capacity."

Draft claim guardrails (how to be careful):
- Always include hardware and model context (e.g., A100-80GB equivalents) and the test date.
- Use ranges, not point estimates, unless backed by at least 3 independent runs and a customer replay.
- Where possible, provide a link to the bench packet and a short methodological note.

Next steps (for this doc):
- Align with Applied ML on model/profile selection and get signoff on the bench harness by EOW.
- Kick off Week 1 runs and reserve perf-harness infra.
- Prepare a simple cost-calculator template and send to field for early feedback.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add example SQL query for deriving session distribution from prod logs.
- Get explicit permission from two pilot customers to use anonymized traces.
- Remove illustrative numbers before any outward-facing collateral unless validated.

Links and refs (internal):
- perf-harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness
- prior throughput research: confluence://perf/throughput-2025-summary
- sales calculator prototype: drive://sheets/unit-econ-calculator-v1

End of note.
